newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Bk cuts loss reserves on loans to Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Bk cuts loss reserves on loans to Philippines.

text.p: Fuji Bank Ltd said on Monday it reduced the amount of special reserves set aside to cover possible losses on loans to the Philippines in fiscal 1996/97, in the belief that the country's economy is showing clear signs of recovery.
A bank official said the bank decreased the reserves to one percent of its loans to the country.
Japanese banks operating internationally are required by the Finance Ministry to set aside special reserves for five years after a country reschedules payments of its borrowings.
The Philippines is one of 20 countries on the list of those that have rescheduled debt payments.

While the ministry requires banks to set aside reserves equivalent to one percent of loans to those countries for five years, the banks have voluntarily set aside special reserves equivalent to 35 percent, banking industry sources said.

With four years having lapsed since the Philippines last rescheduled loan payments and after taking a close look at the country's economy, Fuji decided to cut the amount of the reserves, the official said.
The move will help reduce the cost of lending by the bank to the Philippines and help expand its loans to the country, he said.
Industry sources said other Japanese banks may also take a second look at country risk and set the size of special loan loss reserves on their own.
